title: Concept node
description: The AUTHORED shape of a concept, as committed to /content/nodes. Not the shape the API serves: `tier` and `edges.unlocks` are derived at publish time and must never appear in a file here. See ADR-0002.

id.description: Kebab-case slug. Also the URL: `speculative-decoding` serves at /c/speculative-decoding. Must match the filename.

domain.description: A two-level path, rendered as the mono eyebrow: ["Architecture","Sparsity"] becomes "Architecture / Sparsity". A path, not multi-membership — a concept sits in one place.

bodies.description: The depth toggle. All three ship in the pre-rendered HTML.

emphasis.description: The phrase lifted to violet weight 500, per depth. Each value must be a VERBATIM substring of the matching body — a constraint JSON Schema cannot express, enforced by scripts/validate-content.mjs.

primitive.description: Names an implemented viz primitive — a reusable visual shape, not a per-concept drawing. A typo here would render an empty island, so the set is closed and grows only as primitives land. What each one shows, and which params it reads, is documented in content/schema/README.md.

param_controls.description: The draggable parameter. At most one: the design gives each island a single control, and two would need a layout that does not exist.

caption_engineer.description: Replaces `caption` at the Engineer depth, for a primitive whose Engineer rendering is a different picture (ADR-0005). Optional: omit it and `caption` is shown at every depth, which is right whenever the primitive draws one thing.

edges.description: Only `requires` and `adjacent` are authored. `unlocks` is inverted from `requires` at publish time (ADR-0002) — authoring it would let two files disagree about one fact, so it is rejected here.

citations.description: Real, resolvable sources. Top-level and tier-independent: a node keeps its citations when it is verified. Never nested under `provenance`.

origin.description: Primary sources that predate arXiv and cannot be fetched (ADR-0013). NEVER carries a url — the property does not exist here, so the question of whether these get fetched cannot be reopened. Names where an idea came from; `citations` is what a reader can go and read today, and a node still needs at least one of those.

ref.description: Author-and-year handle, e.g. Graves et al. 2006

doi.description: An identifier, not a link. Validated by pattern and never dereferenced.

review.description: Present iff the node is verified. Its presence IS the tier — adding it in a PR, and merging that PR, is the act of verification (ADR-0002).

provenance.description: Present iff the node is frontier. Drafting metadata only — sources live in top-level `citations`.

oneOf.title: verified — carries a reviewer, and no provenance
frontier — carries drafting provenance, and no reviewer

body.description: Prose. `_` marks a subscript and `^` a superscript, each taking either a run of letters and digits (x_t, d_model, S_ij) or a braced group, which may nest (m_{t−1}, ℝ^{|V|×d_model}). A `{` that does not follow a marker is an ordinary character, so `∈ {0,1}` is safe. Write \_ \^ \{ \} for a literal one. Prefer a Unicode glyph where one exists for the whole construct (β₁, ᵀ, √, ∂) and markup where it does not. Checked by src/lib/notation.test.ts. See ADR-0009.

reviewed.description: Has a human confirmed this relationship? Authored, not derived — the case that matters is an unchecked claim between two verified nodes, which deriving from tier would erase.
